newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Tapie no longer a European deputy.
newsitem.headline: France says Tapie no longer a European deputy.

text.p: France's official journal gave notice on Wednesday that bankrupt ex-businessman and soccer boss Bernard Tapie was no longer a European Parliament Deputy.

The Journal Officiel published a governmment decree signed by Prime Minister Alain Juppe and the ministers for justice, foreign affairs and European affairs, which notes that "the ineligibility of Mr Bernard Tapie puts an end to his mandates as a representative of the European Parliament".

The text of the decree was sent on Tuesday evening to the speaker of the European Parliament and France's ambassador at the institution will give the speaker's office official notification on Thursday in Strasbourg.
A parliamentary committee was due to meet Wednesday or Thursday to rule on the decree. It has the power to overturn the decision, but French officials said this was unlikely.
Tapie, declared by European Union law, the laws of individual member states determine eligibility for the European parliament, French authorities say.

Tapie, target of a blizzard of legal actions over his now-destroyed business empire and the Marseille soccer team he once ran, has been sentenced to jail terms of eight and six months for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match.
He is appealing in both cases to the Supreme Court.
